items.description: Sec. 5.4 only says the design domain is 'as illustrated in Figure 9(a)' and gives no dimensions for the optimization domain. The only size in the text is that of the printed specimens, 120×48×48 mm³. It is not stated that the optimization domain is the same box rather than only the supported span. The text also calls Fig. 9(a) an optimized density field, which conflicts with the caption (9(a) = domain/BCs, 9(b) = density field).
readings: 120 × 48 × 48 box (length × width × height, L:W:H = 5:2:2), identical to the printed specimens
box covering only the support span (e.g. ≈100 × 48 × 48) if the printed specimen overhangs the supports

items.description: The only description is the Fig. 9(a) caption: 'The bottom sides are fixed.' It doesn't say which bottom regions are meant, whether they are edge lines or patches (or how big), or whether they sit at the beam ends or are moved in to a three-point-bending span. The span of the test rig (Fig. 10(a)) isn't given.
readings: full-width line supports along the two bottom end edges (x = 0 and x = L at z = 0)
full-width strips on the bottom face next to each end, of finite length (e.g. 1–3 elements or one unit cell, ≈5–10 % of L)
full-width supports on the bottom face, moved in from the ends to a test span < 120 mm (e.g. 100 mm span)
lower parts of the two end faces (x = 0 and x = L)

items.description: The Fig. 9(a) caption says the bottom sides are 'fixed', but Sec. 5.4 calls the case a three-point bending test, which normally uses simple (roller) supports. The text doesn't say which displacement components are held.
readings: clamped: all three translations fixed at both supports
simply supported: only the vertical displacement fixed at both supports, plus the fewest extra constraints needed to stop rigid-body motion
pin–roller: one support fixed in all translations, the other only vertically

items.entity: load at the centre of the beam top
items.description: The Fig. 9(a) caption says 'the force is uniformly applied at the center of the beam top'. It doesn't say whether this is a line load across the full width at mid-span, pressure on a strip or patch of unknown size, or a point load. No loaded-area size is given.
readings: uniform line load across the full width at mid-span (x = L/2) on the top face
uniform pressure on a full-width mid-span strip of finite length (e.g. 1–3 elements or the loading-nose contact width)
uniform pressure on a small square patch at the centre of the top face (not full width)
single concentrated force at the node at the centre of the top face

items.entity: load at the centre of the beam top
items.description: No value is given for the force used in the optimization (Sec. 5.4 / Fig. 9(a)).
readings: unit total force F = 1
a force at test level (similar to the forces in Fig. 10(b)), exact value unknown

items.description: Sec. 4.3 introduces the base-material stiffness tensor C* but gives no numbers. Sec. 5.4 doesn't name the printing material.
readings: E0 = 1 (normalized)
printed polymer (resin/nylon), E0 ≈ 1.5–3 GPa
printed metal (e.g. Ti-6Al-4V), E0 ≈ 110 GPa

items.description: The Poisson's ratio of the base material (C*, Sec. 4.3) is not given anywhere.

items.entity: stiffness–density law C^H(ρ) for the units of Table 2(a) and 2(c)
items.description: Eq. 26 (Sec. 4.3) models each homogenized coefficient as c_ij(ρ)/c_ij* = a1·e^{a2ρ} − a1. The values of a1 and a2 are not given for either beam unit; Fig. 4(b) only plots curves for a generic symmetric unit. The two beam runs in Sec. 5.4 differ only through this law, and no penalization is specified. A single-material solver therefore needs an assumed interpolation.
readings: linear, no penalization (p = 1), giving a graded density field like Fig. 9(b,c)
SIMP with p = 3
exponential law E(ρ)/E0 = a1(e^{a2ρ} − 1) with an assumed a2 (e.g. 2–4) and a1 = 1/(e^{a2} − 1), separately for each unit
Gibson–Ashby power law E(ρ)/E0 = ρ^2

items.entity: direction dependence (anisotropy) of the homogenized tensor and unit-cell orientation
items.description: Sec. 4.3 says the homogenized tensor of a symmetric unit has 9 independent coefficients (orthotropic). No values are given for the beam units, and the text doesn't say how the unit cells are oriented relative to the beam axes. An isotropic single-material solver cannot represent this without an assumption.
readings: isotropic effective material (ignore the unit's anisotropy)
orthotropic C^H(ρ) with 9 constants per unit, cell axes aligned with the beam axes (values recomputed by homogenizing the units)
cubic-symmetric C^H(ρ) (C11, C12, C44) aligned with the beam axes

items.description: Eq. 27 limits the density to ρ_min ≤ ρ_ijk ≤ ρ_max, the minimum and maximum relative densities of the porous units, but no values are given for the beam.
readings: ρ_min = 0.001, ρ_max = 1 (standard SIMP void/solid bounds)
ρ_min ≈ 0.1–0.2, ρ_max ≈ 0.7–0.9 (range in which the porous unit stays printable and connected)
ρ_min = 0.1, ρ_max = 1

items.description: Sec. 4.3 describes the density as a 3-D B-spline with N_u×N_v×N_w control coefficients 'to ensure smoothness'. This is the only smoothing mentioned (no filter or radius). Neither the number of coefficients nor the B-spline degree is given for the beam, so a structured-grid solver must pick an equivalent filter.
readings: standard density filter, r_min ≈ 1.5 element sizes
density filter with radius about one unit cell or one B-spline knot span (e.g. 12–24 mm)
cubic B-spline density field on a coarse control grid (≈8×4×4 to ≈23×11×11 coefficients) evaluated on the mesh, with no further filter

items.description: Equilibrium is solved with isogeometric analysis (IGA) on the B-spline solid Ω (Sec. 4.3). The number of elements (N_e) or knot spans and the basis degree for the beam are not given.
readings: 40 × 16 × 16 cubic elements (3 mm)
60 × 24 × 24 cubic elements (2 mm)
120 × 48 × 48 cubic elements (1 mm)
IGA with a quadratic or cubic B-spline basis on a coarse knot grid (size unknown)

items.description: Sec. 4.3 says the problem is solved with the OC method, but gives no move limit, damping exponent, stopping tolerance or iteration limit.
readings: move limit 0.2, damping η = 0.5, stop when the largest density change < 0.01
move limit 0.1, η = 0.3, fixed number of iterations (e.g. 100–200)
